Compare a set of sdmTMB model-selection candidates

Source: R/model-selection.R
sdmTMB_selection.Rd

Fits a named list of candidate specifications to identical records and returns a tidy selection table: the full specification of each candidate, its convergence and sanity status, in-sample NLL/AIC with delta-AIC and Akaike weights, and — when cv is on — cross-validated predictive skill expressed per held-out observation. One function covers the usual selection stages (component ranking, dropping fixed effects, family, spatiotemporal structure, mesh resolution), because each is the same operation with a different thing varied.

Usage

sdmTMB_selection(
  candidates,
  data,
  formula = NULL,
  mesh = NULL,
  cutoff = NULL,
  xy_cols = c("X", "Y"),
  family = NULL,
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "iid",
  time = NULL,
  control = sdmTMB::sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 1),
  ...,
  cv = FALSE,
  fold_ids = NULL,
  lfo = FALSE,
  lfo_forecast = 1,
  lfo_validations = 5,
  fit_full = TRUE,
  complete_cases = TRUE,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  cache_prefix = "selection",
  refit = FALSE,
  only = NULL,
  n_workers = 1,
  future_seed = TRUE,
  silent = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

candidates

A named list of candidates. Each element is either a formula, or a list with any of formula, family, spatial, spatiotemporal, mesh, cutoff and time; anything not set falls back to the corresponding argument below. Names become the model column. A candidate that sets its own cutoff overrides a shared mesh, so a mesh-resolution stage is just another candidate list.

data

A data frame with the response, predictors and coordinates.

formula

Default formula for candidates that do not carry one.

mesh

A sdmTMB::make_mesh() mesh shared by all candidates. If NULL, a mesh is built per candidate from cutoff and xy_cols.

cutoff

Default mesh cutoff (km) used when mesh is NULL.

xy_cols

Coordinate columns used to build meshes. Default c("X", "Y").

family

Default sdmTMB::sdmTMB() family. No default: supply it here or per candidate, so the choice is deliberate.

spatial, spatiotemporal, time

Defaults passed to sdmTMB::sdmTMB().

control

An sdmTMB::sdmTMBcontrol() object.

...

Further arguments passed to both sdmTMB::sdmTMB() and sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(). Pass an offset as the name of a column in data, not as a vector — a vector would misalign when complete_cases = TRUE removes rows.

cv

Cross-validation: FALSE (default) for none, or TRUE/an integer number of folds.

fold_ids

Optional fold assignment (a vector, or the name of a column in data) passed to sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(). Use it to hold out spatial blocks (e.g. from blockCV::cv_spatial()) instead of scattered points: random folds measure interpolation, spatially clustered folds measure extrapolation into unsampled ground, which is the harder and more relevant test for a model whose purpose is to integrate over space.

lfo, lfo_forecast, lfo_validations

Leave-future-out cross-validation, passed to sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(). lfo = TRUE scores the model on years it has not seen, which is the question an assessment update actually asks.

fit_full

Fit each candidate once on the whole frame, in addition to any CV? Default TRUE. Needed for AIC, sdmTMB::sanity() and the per-candidate indices in plot(type = "index").

complete_cases

Restrict the data to rows complete for every candidate? Default TRUE. See selection_frame().

cache_dir

Directory for per-candidate .rds caches. NULL (default) disables caching.

cache_prefix

Prefix for cache file names, so several selection stages can share one directory. Default "selection".

refit

Recompute cached candidates? Default FALSE.

only

Optional character vector of candidate names to compute in this call. Candidates outside it are read from the cache if present and skipped otherwise.

n_workers, future_seed

Parallel settings for the CV fits.

silent

Suppress model fitting output? Default TRUE.

verbose

Report progress? Default TRUE.

Value

An object of class sdmTMB_selection: a list with table (the tidy selection table), fits (named list of fitted models or NULLs), cv (named list of sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv() objects, or NULL) and candidates (the resolved specifications). Print it, plot it with plot.sdmTMB_selection(), and query it with best_candidate().

Details

Identical records

With complete_cases = TRUE (the default) the data are passed through selection_frame() first, so every candidate sees the same rows and the likelihood-based columns are comparable. Fit the selected specification to the full data afterwards.

What the table is sorted by, and why you should not rely on it

Rows are ordered by cv_deltaNLL when cross-validation ran and by deltaAIC otherwise. Never read the winner off the first row in downstream code — use best_candidate(), which looks the value up in the column and skips rows that are not comparable.

Comparability

The comparable column is TRUE only for a candidate that fitted, whose Hessian was positive definite, that saw the modal number of records, and — under CV — had every fold resolve and score the modal number of held-out points. Compare only those rows, and do not quote a delta between two candidates unless both are comparable: a likelihood from a fit that has not resolved is not a basis for a comparison, and neither is one computed over a different set of observations.

sdmTMB::sanity() is reported in its own column but does not gate comparability. It is a broader battery of warnings — a range longer than the survey domain, a random-field SD collapsing to zero, a large gradient — that flags a model worth thinking about rather than one whose likelihood is meaningless; gating on it would quietly drop the best-fitting candidate from the comparison. Read it, and treat a sanity = FALSE winner as a reason to simplify rather than as a row to ignore.

Cost

A cross-validated candidate costs k fits (plus one more when fit_full = TRUE, which is needed for AIC, sanity and per-candidate indices). Cross-validating a long ladder is therefore usually the wrong order of work: rank all candidates by AIC first (cv = FALSE), then cross-validate a shortlist taken from that ranking with best_candidate(). With cache_dir set and the same cache_prefix, the second call reuses the whole-frame fits from the first and pays only for the folds.

Caching and resumability

cache_dir writes two files per candidate — the whole-frame fit and the cross-validation separately — so an interrupted run resumes instead of starting over, and a cross-validated call under the same cache_prefix reuses the fits an earlier AIC ladder already paid for instead of repeating them. only restricts a call to named candidates so a long ladder can be spread over several R sessions (a large spatiotemporal fit can exhaust memory when a dozen of them accumulate in one process).

See also

selection_frame(), best_candidate(), plot.sdmTMB_selection(), sdmTMB_cv_summary(), compare_models()

Examples

# \donttest{
cands <- list(
  "Year only" = density ~ 0 + as.factor(year),
  "+ depth" = density ~ 0 + as.factor(year) + depth_scaled,
  "No spatiotemporal" = list(spatiotemporal = "off")
)
sel <- sdmTMB_selection(
  cands, data = sdmTMB::pcod,
  formula = density ~ 0 + as.factor(year) + depth_scaled,
  cutoff = 25, family = sdmTMB::tweedie(), time = "year",
  spatial = "on", spatiotemporal = "iid"
)
#> Candidate 'Year only': fitting.
#> Candidate '+ depth': fitting.
#> Candidate 'No spatiotemporal': fitting.
sel
#> <sdmTMB_selection> 3 candidates, AIC only 
#> 
#>              model    n crashed converged sanity      AIC  deltaAIC   AICweight
#>            + depth 2143   FALSE      TRUE  FALSE 13086.73   0.00000 1.00000e+00
#>          Year only 2143   FALSE      TRUE  FALSE 13154.57  67.84453 1.85245e-15
#>  No spatiotemporal 2143   FALSE      TRUE  FALSE 13234.01 147.28353 1.04181e-32
#>  comparable
#>        TRUE
#>        TRUE
#>        TRUE
#> 
#> 3 of 3 rows are comparable.
#> Best (AIC): + depth
#> 3 comparable row(s) fail sanity(): they are still compared, but check
#> them before trusting the winner.
plot(sel)

best_candidate(sel)
#> [1] "+ depth"
# }
